title: Postpartum haemorrhage
stem: Resus 2. A 28-year-old woman (G2P2) gave birth at home 40 minutes ago; the placenta was delivered by the midwife. She is bleeding heavily, soaking pads and the sheet. HR 124, BP 88/54, RR 24, SpO2 97%, GCS 15. Her baby is well with her partner.
notes:
Checked against RCOG Green-top Guideline 52 (Postpartum haemorrhage), the WOMAN trial (tranexamic acid), WHO 2023 recommendations and the E-MOTIVE bundle (NEJM 2023), and NICE NG235 (Intrapartum care, 2023).

Major PPH: over 1000 mL or signs of shock. Call for help (senior obstetrician, anaesthetist, midwife), activate the major haemorrhage protocol, two large-bore cannulae, bloods (FBC, coagulation, fibrinogen, crossmatch 4 units), warmed fluids limited to about 2 L crystalloid before blood (RCOG), O-negative if needed. Tranexamic acid 1 g IV within 3 hours of birth, second 1 g after 30 minutes if bleeding continues (WOMAN). Your notes omit tranexamic acid; it is scored here.

The 4 Ts: Tone (commonest), Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin. Tone: rub up a contraction (fundal massage), bimanual compression, empty the bladder; oxytocin 5 IU slow IV (may repeat), ergometrine 0.5 mg IV/IM (not in hypertension), oxytocin infusion 40 IU in 500 mL at 125 mL/h, carboprost 250 microgram IM every 15 minutes (max 8 doses; caution in asthma), misoprostol 800 microgram sublingual; then balloon tamponade and surgery. Check the placenta is complete and look for tears.

Your notes' structure matches this; they start with a 1 L Hartmann's bolus, which is acceptable in the RCOG limit. E-MOTIVE adds early detection by measured blood loss and a bundle given together (massage, oxytocics, tranexamic acid, fluids, examination and escalation).

steps.label: Call and prepare
steps.hint: Obstetric emergency call, major haemorrhage protocol, two cannulae, bloods, warm fluids.

opts.t: Obstetric emergency call: senior obstetrician, anaesthetist, midwife
Activate the major haemorrhage protocol; O-negative available
Two large-bore cannulae; FBC, clotting, fibrinogen, crossmatch 4 units, gas
opts.mark: Access and bloods including fibrinogen and crossmatch

opts.t: Weigh the pads and sheet to measure blood loss
Lie her flat, oxygen, keep her warm

steps.label: Assess
steps.hint: Quick history, the uterus, the perineum, the placenta.

History.t: Placenta complete? Any tears? Risk factors?
History.r: Midwife: placenta looked complete. Long labour, big baby (4.3 kg). No known bleeding disorder.
History.mark: Takes a focused history for the 4 Ts

Abdomen.r: Soft, boggy uterus at the umbilicus; blood gushes when you press.

Perineum.r: Small first-degree tear, not bleeding much.

steps.label: Treat the tone
steps.hint: Rub up a contraction, empty the bladder, oxytocin, ergometrine, infusion, bimanual compression; tranexamic acid.

opts.t: Fundal massage to rub up a contraction
Urinary catheter to empty the bladder
Tranexamic acid 1 g IV over 10 minutes
opts.mark: Tranexamic acid within 3 hours of birth

opts.t: Ergometrine 0.5 mg IV (BP is not high)
opts.mark: Ergometrine, checking there is no hypertension

opts.t: Oxytocin infusion 40 IU in 500 mL at 125 mL/h
opts.r: The uterus firms up. Bleeding slows.

opts.t: Still bleeding: bimanual compression while carboprost 250 microgram IM is drawn up

opts.r: Ergometrine is contraindicated in hypertension and pre-eclampsia.

steps.label: Fluids and blood
steps.hint: Warm crystalloid, then blood; keep her warm.

opts.t: Warm Hartmann's up to 2 L while blood comes; then red cells and plasma per protocol
opts.mark: Limits crystalloid and moves to blood
opts.r: Midwife Kong: Blood running through the warmer.

opts.t: Fibrinogen above 2 g/L: cryoprecipitate or fibrinogen concentrate if lower
Six litres of saline until the pressure normalises
opts.r: Dilutional coagulopathy. Blood and products early.

steps.label: If bleeding continues
steps.hint: Theatre: examination under anaesthesia, balloon tamponade, surgery or radiology.

opts.t: Obstetrician: to theatre for examination, balloon tamponade, then compression suture or interventional radiology if needed
opts.mark: Escalates to surgical and radiological options

wrong: Mild asthma on a salbutamol inhaler

qs.a: 1 g IV within 3 h; repeat after 30 min if needed
wrong: 1 g IV only if bleeding continues beyond 6 hours
1 g orally three times daily for 5 days
8 mg oral as a single dose

badge.name: Rub It Up
badge.flavor: Tone first. Oxytocin, TXA, and escalate early.
